userStories.title: [E12] Zone keys that fit the outbox: ZoneHealthChanged and every event keyed by zone
userStories.description: outbox_message.message_key is varchar(200) (script 0011), but a zone key <site>/<queue zone name> can reach 218 characters (a site of up to 17, a zone name of up to 200). userStories.title: [E3] Stream on event time: watermarks from the events, not the batch's arrival
userStories.description: Owner decision 2026-10-10 (ARV-104j finding F1, with F4). In the live pipeline about 40 percent of a busy lane's crossings were dropped as late: Ingest splits a push into per-topic batches and Stream moves each zone's clock to the receive time of each batch, so a one-minute push carrying events up to 61 seconds old turns its older crossings late against the 30-second lateness, and the recomputation requests this raises are never carried out in the live path. Stream moves each zone by the events' own time: a zone's watermark is the latest event time it has seen less the allowed lateness (configurable per site, by default at least the push interval); bins close when the watermark passes their end; an event older than the watermark is late as today. F4: an outage ends at the start of the minute the first push after it covers, so the bin after the outage is judged again. The golden replay is updated (owner approval 2026-10-10). Epic: Queue state engine. CWEs to review: CWE-501, CWE-120.
acceptanceCriteria: The queue state engine and the live Stream path advance each zone by event time (watermark per zone, allowed lateness per site with a default of at least the push interval), deterministic for a given event sequence whatever the batch boundaries; the pure engine keeps no I/O
A one-minute push of events up to 61 seconds old loses no crossing as late; a genuinely late event (older than the watermark) is still counted late and requests a recomputation as today
F4: an outage ends at the start of the minute the first push after it covers; the S-17 outage of seed 9303 leaves the 18:30 bin judged

userStories.title: [E6] Dead letters: text PostgreSQL accepts, a per-topic relay hold and a shutdown budget that fits
userStories.description: From the ARV-171 security review (PASS, 2026-10-13), three non-blocking findings. (1) A NUL character or a lone surrogate in a record's key, a header name or value, or the error message makes the keep fail (PostgreSQL text refuses 0x00 in message_key, and CAST AS jsonb refuses \u0000 and unpaired surrogates in the payload), so such a record still ends on ARV-166's unacknowledged path; it needs a buggy or hostile Kafka producer, which is what the unreadable path is for. (3) The app charts set no terminationGracePeriodSeconds (Kubernetes default 30 s) and no host sets HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout (.NET default 30 s), while one in-flight message can need the rest of its retry schedule (at most 3 x 5 s), the keep (at most 10 s) and the consumer close. A .dlq.v1 row whose send fails with a broker error holds back only its topic for the rest of the relay pass instead of ending the pass, so domain rows keep draining; a domain row's failure still ends the pass as today

The consuming hosts' pods set terminationGracePeriodSeconds 60 and the hosts set HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout to about 50 s (configurable, validated), so the clean path (the rest of the retry schedule, the keep, the consumer close) fits; chart render tests assert both; wiki 10 or the deployment guide names the budget

userStories.title: [E18] Web requests bound to the account that started them
userStories.description: Follow-up from the ARV-104c security review (2026-10-09, Low). Api.ts recovers a 401 by refreshing the session and sending the request again. A request started by one account that is still in flight when that account signs out and another signs in on the same browser is then sent again under the second account, or its recovery signs the second account out; an MFA step-up can be shown to the second account for the first account's action. ARV-104c closed this for the capture calls only (asSubject). The server still applies the second account's permissions and site scope and audits it, so the exposure is small, but a request must never change hands. Epic: Accounts and sessions. CWEs to review: CWE-384, CWE-863, CWE-501.
acceptanceCriteria: Api.ts request() records auth.subject when a call starts and uses it as the default for asSubject: once a different account or none is signed in, the request is not sent, not sent again after a refresh, and does not trigger the 401 recovery (no refresh, no sessionEnded, no MFA step-up)
